name: No Good Deed Goes Unpunished
desc: Shares the first seven bots with 'The Marlin'. Climb up in the cave and traverse out on the face. Then go straight up and to the left. All titanium bolts The lower part of the climb needs to be cleaned on toprope to prevent big swings into the trees.

name: The Marlin
desc: Shares the first seven bolts with 'No Good Deed Goes Unpunished'. Climb up in the cave and traverse out on the face, then follow the bolts to the right. Pass the midway anchor and keep going towards the tufa system on the right. All titanium bolts Should be cleaned by the top rope follower to prevent big swings into the trees. Can be climbed in two short pitches or as a single pitch (with a 70m rope, 60m may not be enough).

name: It / Up

setter: Rock and Sun & Desiree Massiah-Verbeek, Mar 2019 (FA: Desiree Massiah-Verbeek, Mar 2019)

name: Wind Burn / Sun

setter: Rock and Sun & Desiree Massiah-Verbeek (FA: Rock and Sun, Mar 2019)

name: Organ Grinder
desc: Usually climbed as one pitch. All titanium bolts. After the P1 anchors, share 2-3 bolts with Hiroshi’s Revenge before attacking the sharp looking juggy arete, clipping bolts on the left side of the lip as you head up.
setter: Sam Lightner, Greg Collum & Rock and Sun, 1993

name: Hiroshi's Revenge
desc: Starts with the first pitch of 'Organ Grinder', then continues up, via tufa onto the wall. Mix of titanium bolts and slings.
setter: Rock and Sun & Desiree Massiah-Verbeek, Mar 2019 (FA: Rock and Sun, Mar 2019)

name: Inaka
desc: This route is a mess. Don't do it. There is a lot of loose rock and sharpies that can cut your rope. Also no rebolting of the upper pitches since 1996. Take 15 quickdraws and extra threads if you're really keen... The first pitch is now 'Hiroshi's Revenge'.
warnings: Rock: There is a lot of loose rock and sharpies that can cut your rope.

name: Continental Drifters
desc: Good but not as good as 'Lord of the Thais' and 'The King and I'. Take 14 quickdraws. 1. 6 old bolts. First two pitches are not rebolted. Better access P3 from 'Monkey Love'. 2. 7 old bolts. See P1. 3. Straight up over the bulge. 8 titanium bolts. 4. Left towards the cave. 12 titanium bolts. 5. Sharp rock to the top. 7 titanium bolts. From the anchor of P3, it is a 60m rap to the ground with two 60m ropes.
setter: Sam Lightner, Volker Schöffl & Gerd Schöffl, 1994
warnings: Fixed Gear: 6 old bolts. First two pitches are not rebolted.
Fixed Gear: 7 old bolts.
Rock: Sharp rock to the top.

name: Monkey Love
desc: Exposed line through the tufa system. Titanium bolts and slings.
setter: Greg Collum & Larissa Collum, 1992 (Maint: Rock and Sun, Jan 2023)

name: Out of Sticks
desc: Original grade was 7a+. Upgraded to 7b after a hold broke off. Shares the start with 'Caveman', then left straight over the bulge. 8 titanium bolts, 1 sling.
setter: Sam Lightner, Gerd Schöffl & Volker Schöffl, 1994

name: Caveman
desc: Shares the start with 'Out of Sticks', then further right up the crack. Can be climbed as one pitch. 11 titanium bolts, 1 sling.

name: Twenty Kilos of Steel
desc: Access route to the big cave connecting 'Thaiwand Wall' and 'Escher World'. 1 titanium bolt, 4 slings.

name: Circus Oz
desc: Popular and will get you as far of the deck as you will get in this area. Take 14 quickdraws and two 60m ropes. Be aware that the upper pitches are not rebolted with titanium! 1. Same first pitch as 'Lord of the Thais', straight up on the right side of the big cave. 7 titanium bolts, 3 slings. 2. Stay left of the bolts, up into the cave. Find the anchor just right above the anchor of 'Continental Drifters' P2. 4 titanium bolts, 5 slings. 3. Crux pitch. Quite fun if you have the means. Move left, then up over the bulge. 7 stainless steel glue-in bolts, 4 slings. 4. Sharp rock to the anchors of 'Lord of the Thais'. Take care. A fall on the last bit of the last pitch could be very dangerous, because there is some sharp rock and you're falling into a dihedral. 7 stainless steel glue-in bolts, 4 slings. Descend via the anchors of 'Lord of the Thais'. Three raps to the ground with two 60m ropes. Backclip to stay on the wall!
setter: M Matheson, G Tempest, El Gordo & RD Smith, 1994
warnings: Fixed Gear: Be aware that the upper pitches are not rebolted with titanium!
Fixed Gear: 7 stainless steel glue-in bolts, 4 slings.
Rock: Sharp rock to the anchors of 'Lord of the Thais'.
Rock: A fall on the last bit of the last pitch could be very dangerous, because there is some sharp rock and you're falling into a dihedral.

name: Lord of the Thais
desc: One of the best routes in Thailand, maybe the world? Take 15 quickdraws and two 60m ropes. 1. Same first pitch as 'Circus Oz', straight up on the right side of the big cave. 7 titanium bolts, 3 slings. 2. Straight up over two bulges, then slightly left to the anchor on a big ledge. 8 titanium bolts, 4 slings. 3. Slightly left and straight up. 11 titanium bolts. 4. Towards the right through steep rock. 10 titanium bolts. 5. Short pitch to the left on sharp rock, just to reach the top. 2 titanium bolts, 1 sling. Descend by rapping down three times with two 60m ropes. Backclip to stay on the wall!
setter: Sam Lightner, Greg Collum & Larissa Collum, 1992
warnings: Rock: Short pitch to the left on sharp rock, just to reach the top.

name: Mala Mujer
desc: Good vertical climb on tufas and big holds. 9 titanium bolts, 3 slings.

name: Getting to Know You / Etcetera, Etcetera, Etcetera
desc: Awesone route!! the anchor is after the sling up to the left. All titanium bolts.

name: The Sluggard Prince
desc: Shares anchors with 'Sanuked'. Not rebolted with titanium. 1 expansion bolt, 12 slings.
warnings: Fixed Gear: Not rebolted with titanium. 1 expansion bolt, 12 slings.

name: The King and I
desc: A fun climb, especially the second pitch. Take 14 quickdraws and two 60m ropes. 1. Also a great single-pitch climb. Steep and pumpy. Alternatively, it is possible to climb 'The Sluggard Prince' and traverse right to the anchor. 12 titanium bolts. 2. Pass the midway anchor and climb up to the next anchor inside a small cave. 11 titanium bolts. 3. Left out of the belay cave. Again, pass an old anchor and climb straight up, then left to the anchor of 'Lord of the Thais' P4. 11 titanium bolts. 4. Same as P5 of 'Lord of the Thais', sharp rock to the top. 2 titanium bolts, 1 sling. Descend via the anchors of 'Lord of the Thais'. Three raps to the ground with two 60m ropes. Backclip to stay on the wall!
setter: Sam Lightner, Jacob Valdez & Somporn Suebhait, 1992
warnings: Rock: Same as P5 of 'Lord of the Thais', sharp rock to the top.

name: Sanuked
desc: Starts at the top of 'The Sluggard Prince' and shares the anchor with P2 of 'The King and I'. Straight up for 3 clips, then crosses over P2 of 'The King and I'. Continues up right to under a small roof, then left and up to the belay cave. From the anchor it is a 60m rap to the ground. Very sustained climbing. 6 bolts, 8 slings.

name: Fit to Be Thaid
desc: A little sharp but otherwise fun climbing

name: Fit to Be Thaid (Extension)
desc: Linkup from the anchors of 'Fit to Be Thaid' to the anchors of 'The King and I'. Only protected by slings. Be prepared to replace.

name: Approach Pitch

name: The Red Line
desc: The leftmost line on red-coated featured rock. All titanium bolts. 1. After the shared start take the left line of bolts to the left anchor on the belay ledge. 12 bolts. 2. Up and left towards the pumpy crux right before the anchor. 10 bolts.

name: Crystal Flame
desc: The classic line at 'Candlestick Wall'. All titanium bolts. 1. Take the righthand variation of the first pitch, which leads you to the right of the two belay anchors in a small cave. 12 bolts. 2. From the belay ledge,take the line straight up along crystal-lined pockets to the anchor below the topout tunnel. 11 bolts. 3. Chimney up the tunnel to reach the top of the Thaiwand. 1 sling.
setter: Drew Spaulding, Brian Warshow & Cameron Fairburn, 2000

name: The Candlestick
desc: Great overhanging second pitch. All titanium bolts. 1. Take the righthand variation of the first pitch to reach the right anchor in the cave. 12 bolts. 2. Move out right of the belay cave. Where the route splits follow the left bolt line. To the right is 'Thai Stick'. 9 bolts, 11 slings. On descent, reclip the draws on P2 to avoid being stuck in free space. When abseiling P1, change over at the rap station - 70m rope does not reach the start.

name: Thai Stick
desc: Shares the start with 'The Candlestick', then takes the line further to the right through beautiful rock. All titanium bolts. 1. Take the righthand variation of the first pitch to reach the right anchor in the cave. 12 bolts. 2. Move out right of the belay cave. Where the route splits follow the right bolt line. 14 bolts.

name: Attacktit

name: Genesis
desc: The leftmost route on this crag. Also the only one that continues past the lip of the roof and up the leaning headwall, all the way to the jungle. Not rebolted with titanium, 9 stainless steel glue-ins, 2 slings.
setter: Björn Alber, Nantawan Alber & Henrik Bolander, 2010
warnings: Fixed Gear: Not rebolted with titanium, 9 stainless steel glue-ins, 2 slings.

name: Tough Trip Through Paradise
desc: Warning Fixed Gear: Ware on sling Climbs the short roof a few meters right of 'Genesis' to an anchor just above the lip. 4 titanium bolts, 1 sling. There seems to be the option of doing linkups via the rail 1-2 m before the lip.

name: Khun Bar
desc: Two meters left of 'Black Diamond'. Bouldery. Titanium bolts.

name: Black Diamond
desc: Dyno crux on the steep black rock a few meters left of 'Little Shit'. Always wet and slimy, impossible to climb after rain. Titanium bolts.

name: Little Shit
desc: The lefthand 6c taking a rail/flake for the steepest bit. Reportedly not very good, but with this grade and location it was always going to get heaps of traffic. Shares anchors with 'Princess Eyes'. All titanium bolts.

name: Princess Eyes
desc: The righthand 6c, this time getting through the steep bit on fingery pockets. This one is also supposed to be pretty average. Shares anchors with 'Little Shit'. Titanium bolts.

name: Titanium from Hell / Tales of Power
desc: Just left behind the tufa hanging down to 2m off the sand. Juggy rail to some tricky moves around the bulge then stem up the left side of the hanging tufa system. All titanium bolts. Originally named 'Tales of Power' at grade 7c. Rebolted a little further right to an easier line. Some guidebooks kept the original name.

name: Don't Buy Toys
desc: Pockety steep start into the big huecos, then up the right side of the tufa system. The 4th bolt is actually on the side of the tufa. All titanium bolts.

name: New Way
desc: Linkup. Shares the start with 'Don't Buy Toys', then continue right into 'Mekong Haze' after the 3rd bolt. Titanium bolts.

name: Mekong Haze
desc: Just right of 'Don't Buy Toys'. Bit of a squeeze but looks great! All titanium bolts.

name: Might as Well Hurl
desc: Right of 'Mekong Haze'. Awesome moves! A short draw or single carabiner on the 2nd bolt is good at softening the swing back onto the belayer's rope for falls off the first crux. All titanium bolts.

name: Up to You
desc: The righmost route on the eye-catching pocketed section of rock, and possibly the best here. Shares the start with 'Half Dragon' and 'Hot Dragon'. All titanium bolts.

name: Half Dragon
desc: Righthand finish variation of 'Up to You'. Veers right before the last bolt to a separate anchor a bit higher up. 30 degrees the whole way. All titanium bolts. The original line was called 'Hot Dragon' and continued up right for another 5m at 8b grade. The old bolts have been chopped and the new shorter and easier route was called 'Half Dragon'. Some guidebooks kept the original name though.
warnings: Fixed Gear: The old bolts have been chopped and the new shorter and easier route was called 'Half Dragon'.

name: Hot Dragon
desc: Closed Original line that was recycled into 'Half Dragon'. The old bolts have been chopped.
warnings: Fixed Gear: The old bolts have been chopped.

name: Left of Cleft
desc: Subtract 2 grades if your span is 190cm+, or add two grades if it's less! Lovely rock, cool moves, all ruined by the last move. Over the bulge, then climb the easy cleft for 8m onto the steep wall just left of the cleft. 7 titanium bolts, 2 slings. Some guidebooks list this route as 'No Name'.

name: Em & Ems
desc: Just right of the cleft, the leftmost line on the Money Maker pillar. Slightly grungy black rock at times. Grade varies between 5 and 6a in different guidebooks. The fixed hangers are shiny, but beware.

name: Lak Kai
desc: Just left of 'Money Maker'. Grade varies between 5 and 6a in different guidebooks. Titanium bolts and slings. Bolt plate missing before anchors, long run out and slings have seen better days.

name: Money Maker
desc: Start on the left side of the Money Maker pillar and go straight up. Top half is nice and delicate. 4 titanium bolts, 1 sling.

name: Phra-Nang Princess
desc: Shares the start with 'Money Maker', then trend right. Titanium bolts. Originally this route was a 90m multi-pitch. Only the first pitch was rebolted and now carries the name.

name: Small Change
desc: Start on the front of the column, then straight up into 'Phra-Nang Princess'.

name: Back To Mani / Cave
desc: Steepish start up the corner on the right side of the pillar. Finish inside a cave. 1 titanium bolt, 4 slings.

name: Top-Roped
desc: Climbs uo right of 'Back to Mani', all the way to the top of the pillar, sharing anchor with 'Money Maker'. No bolts, climb toprope.

name: Fertilite / Princess Cave
desc: Starts in the corner right of the Money Maker pillar and climbs up right onto the face. All titanium bolts. The original line was one of the first routes on the Phra-Nang peninsula and climbed on further right for a total length of 35m. However, due to the proximity to the Princess Cave and the many tourists below on the beach, only the first half has been rebolted and the original bolts have been chopped.
setter: Thierry Renault, Marlie Walsh & Kurt Albert †, 1989

name: Crystal Prison
desc: Old rusty expansion bolts. Do not climb!
warnings: Fixed Gear: Old rusty expansion bolts.
